bullets.title: The Fog of War
bullets.note:
This documentary has been recommended to me countless times (the last person
was Morgan Spurlock, during [our podcast
together](http://www.fourhournewsletter.com/click.html?x=a62e&lc=wOq&mc=e&s=bomwH&u=w&y=C&),
and I finally bit the bullet. It’s… amazing. At [98% on Rotten
Tomatoes](http://www.fourhournewsletter.com/click.html?x=a62e&lc=wOU&mc=e&s=bomwH&u=w&y=y&),
I shouldn’t have been surprised. The synopsis: Former Secretary of Defense
Robert S. McNamara is the sole focus of documentarian Errol Morris' The Fog of
War, a film that not only analyzes McNamara's controversial decisions during
the first half of the Vietnam War, but also his childhood upbringing, his
education at Berkeley and Harvard, his involvement in World War II, and his
later years as president of the World Bank. Culling footage from almost 20
hours of interviews with the Secretary, Morris details key moments from
McNamara's career, including most important lessons learned.

bullets.title: The Tail End
bullets.creator: Tim Urban — If you only read one article this month, please make it this one
bullets.note:

It was recommended to me by [Matt
Mullenweg](http://www.fourhournewsletter.com/click.html?x=a62e&lc=wa4&mc=e&s=bomwH&u=w&y=r&)
and uses diagrams to really underscore how short life is. Here’s just one gem:
"It turns out that when I graduated from high school, I had already used up
93% of my in-person parent time. I’m now enjoying the last 5% of that time.
We’re in the tail end.” Might be time for you (and me) to rethink our
priorities. Read this as a catalyst.
